newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ALL ROADS LEADING TO PORT HEDLAND CLOSED
All main roads into Port Hedland are closed, isolating the Pilbara town.
The North-West Coastal Highway is blocked at Roebourne, to the south of Port Hedland, and Broome to the north.
Other arteries closed include the Newman to Hedland road and the Marble Bar and Woodie Woodie Roads.
Shipping in Port Hedland has also been affected with one iron ore vessel tied up at Nelson Point and three ships taking shelter out to sea.
NEW STUDY FINDS FEW YOUNG CYCLISTS WEAR HELMETS
A new study has found that young cyclists should wear helmets when they're riding both on the road and off the road.
The study -- by the Tasmanian Injury Surveillance and Prevention Project -- used data from more than 90-thousand bicycle related injuries.
Project co-ordinator, Glenn Jacobson, says the study found that more than half the children under the age of 10, who were taken to hospital, received some sort of head injury.
Mr Jacobson says only 29 per cent of young cyclists in hospital reported using a helmet.
Dr Jacobson is concerned that most of the accidents happened off road, where he says there appears to be a perception that helmets aren't needed.
TALKS OVER JOCKEYS DISPUTE CONTINUING
Talks are continuing today between racing officials seeking a resolution of the dispute over jockeys minimum pay rates.
Jockeys in three states have been fined thousands of dollars for failing to meet race commitments on Saturday.
The jockeys took nation-wide industrial action in support of a claim for a new base rate of 130 dollars per ride, doubling the current minimum payment.
Representatives of the jockeys and the principal clubs are now expected to take part in a conference on pay rates likely to start on February the 3rd.
NEW VOYAGER TRIAL NEXT WEEK
The 1964 Voyager disaster will be at the centre of a new trial in the New South Wales Supreme Court next week.
57-year-old William McLean, who survived when the destroyer, H-M-A-S Voyager collided with H-M-A-S Melbourne off the New South Wales south coast is suing the Commonwealth for the second time.
Mr McLean, who has throat cancer, was last year awarded one-point-seven-million-dollars in compensation, but a retrial was ordered when the Commonwealth successfully appealed against the decision.
Mr McLean claims that after the accident, the Navy failed to treat his acute anxiety, which led him to smoke and drink heavily.
SNOWING IN THE VICTORIAN ALPS
A sudden cold snap brought snow to the Victorian alps this morning, with tempertures diving below zero.
Summer workers at the Mount Hotham and Falls Creek ski resorts say there are good flurries of snow at both resorts. - - - -
SECOND ORION GOING OUT TO JOIN RESCUE
The Air Force is sending another Orion aircraft from Adelaide to join the three others already operating out of Perth, in the search for a lone yachtsman in the Southern Ocean off Western Australia.
The Defence Department's Colonel Andy Reynolds, told ABC Radio that an Orion yesterday dropped a life raft to 29-year-old Theiry Dubois.
Colonel Reynolds says he managed to climb into the life raft but he turned it around towards the five-metre swell and it started sinking.
